svg.aria-label: How to write ન: 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ન
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ન (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ન animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates ન as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left of the small loop, circles clockwise around that loop, then continues right across the long shoulder to the right-spine junction. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small left loop, long shoulder, tall right spine, and lower foot, but its printed loop is wider and its shoulder and spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-shoulder-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently.
